draft.title: Asking an investigation question
card: An investigation question is the question you set out to answer when you research an economic or business issue. A good one guides what you look for.
Open
it cannot be answered with just yes or no. It needs explaining, such as "How does..." or "Why has...".
Focused
it is about one issue, in a clear place or group. "How has the price of eggs changed in Australian supermarkets?" is focused. "How does the whole economy work?" is too wide.
Evidence

it can be answered with information you can find, such as prices, sales figures or survey results. A question about what is best or what is right depends on opinion, so evidence alone cannot settle it.
draft.remember: A good investigation question is open, focused on one issue, and answerable with evidence.

a.q: Which of these is the best investigation question for a Year 7 student studying an economic issue?
opts: How have school canteen prices changed over two years?
Is the school canteen good?
Is the canteen cheaper than the shop?
How does every business in Australia set prices?
a.why: The first question is open, focused on one issue and can be answered with price records. "Is the school canteen good?" is a closed yes or no question, and it depends on opinion. Asking about every business is far too wide.
a.clue: Look for a question that is open, narrow and can be checked.

b.q: Mia plans to investigate a bakery in Ballarat. Which investigation question is open, focused and answerable with evidence?
opts: Why have bread sales at Mia's Ballarat bakery changed this year?
Does the Ballarat bakery sell the best bread in Victoria?
Is the Ballarat bakery busy on Saturdays?
How do all bakeries in the world make money?
b.why: Sales records and customer surveys can show why bread sales changed, and the question needs explaining, not yes or no. "Best bread" is a matter of opinion, so evidence alone cannot settle it. The Saturday question is focused and can be checked, but it is closed because it only needs yes or no.
b.clue: Check each question for all three features, not just one.
